item.title: Matos accepts Swansea fans' anger over shock exit
item.description: Vitor Matos was due to celebrate a year in charge at Swansea next Tuesday [AFP via Getty Images] Vitor Matos admits he knows why Swansea City fans will be angry following his sudden departure from the club. The Portuguese head coach quit the Championship side this week for the top job at French League 1 club RC Strasbourg. His move took Swansea by complete surprise, just a week before marking his first year in charge with the club sixth in the table and having signed a new contract until 2030 in July. Speaking at his first press conference at Strasbourg, Matos admitted he does not "expect any goodwill" from the Welsh club's supporters. He said: "One situation I need to address is Swansea. It was a really hard and tough decision to leave the club mainly because from the first day, they treated me with all respect and care – me and my family. "So it was a really tough decision to leave and that's why I needed to thank everyone there. "Saying that, I really don't expect any good will from the Swansea supporters after my decision. I understand they are angry with that, but it's a club that I love that I worked every day to make better, me and my staff." Listen: Ashley Williams' first press conference back at Swansea A badly timed shock - the story of Matos' Swans exit Listen to the latest Swansea City news Swansea are expecting a compensation package of about £5m and have appointed former players Ashley Williams, Leon Britton, Joe Allen and Kris O'Leary to take temporary charge before Saturday's league fixture against West Bromwich Albion. "To the staff and to the players I have no doubt they will succeed in the future," said Matos. "I have no doubt that the manager will go into the office and make the club move forward and fulfill the dreams of the club." He added: "I'm really proud to be Racing's next manager. This is a wonderful club that deserves all thee respect of everyone."

item.title: Nebraska Has One Final Chance to Change the Recruiting Narrative Against Ohio State
item.description: Trae Taylor headlines a group of 19 recruits expected in Lincoln as Nebraska looks to deliver a statement victory in its final home game of the season. Nebraska’s final home game against Ohio State carries significance far beyond the result on Saturday afternoon. For the seniors, it represents an emotional farewell to Memorial Stadium. For the coaching staff, it is another opportunity to demonstrate that the program is heading in the right direction. And for the 19 recruits expected in Lincoln, it is a chance to see whether Nebraska can finally turn its promise into results against one of college football’s heavyweight programs. There is no getting around the fact that this has been a frustrating season for the Huskers. Nebraska has shown enough to suggest that the gap between itself and the Big Ten’s elite is narrowing, but competing with those programs and actually beating them are two very different things. With the 2027 recruiting class shaping up to be one of Nebraska’s strongest in recent memory, Saturday represents another important opportunity to reinforce the belief that Matt Rhule is building something special in Lincoln. Trae Taylor’s Return Is a Massive Positive Perhaps the most encouraging name on the visitor list is five-star quarterback commit Trae Taylor. Taylor has become the centrepiece of Nebraska’s 2027 recruiting class, both through his ability on the field and his leadership off it. His return to Lincoln is particularly significant given the uncertainty surrounding Nebraska’s offense. The Huskers have struggled to find consistency offensively, and the firing of offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen has raised legitimate questions about the direction of the unit. For a five-star quarterback, the identity of the offensive coordinator, the system he will operate in and the development opportunities available are understandably important considerations. Taylor would be well within his rights to seek reassurance about Nebraska’s offensive future. Instead, his continued involvement with the program is an encouraging indication that his commitment extends beyond any single coach. Taylor has also played an important role in bringing Nebraska’s 2027 recruiting class together. The relationships he has developed with fellow commitments could prove invaluable as the Huskers approach another potentially turbulent offseason. He will be joined by seven other 2027 commits, including four-star safeties Tory Pittman III and Corey Hadley Jr. The presence of such a significant group of committed players provides an opportunity for Nebraska to reinforce those relationships while allowing the recruits to spend valuable time together. Keeping this class intact must be one of the coaching staff’s biggest priorities. item.title: 3 things about Denver Broncos heading into Week 11
item.description: (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders head to play at the Denver Broncos on Sunday. Kickoff is set for 1:25 p.m. PT. Here are three things to know about the Broncos: They’re rolling: The 7-2 Broncos have won five straight games. The Broncos have also had the Raiders’ number lately as they have beaten them four consecutive games. That came directly after the Raiders won eight straight games over Denver. They’re struggling on the ground: The Broncos aren’t running the ball well. They are averaging 81.4 yards a game on the ground and just 3.7 yards per carry. The Raiders’ defense has been gutted by the run, but they may get a break this week against the Broncos. Bo Nix gets hot when he has to: Denver quarterback Bo Nix isn’t perfect, but he gets hot when the game is on the line. They have three fourth-quarter comebacks wins this season and have won 16 straight one-score games.

item.title: Why Miami QB Darian Mensah Wasn’t A 2026 Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award Finalist Over Arch Manning
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The 2026 Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award finalists were announced on Friday, with many of the nation’s top quarterbacks in the mix for the honor. However, there was one major surprise for college football fans with the Miami Hurricanes ‘ Darian Mensah kept off in favor of the Texas Longhorns ‘ Arch Manning. No one could argue against the inclusions of CJ Carr ( Notre Dame Fighting Irish ), Devon Dampier ( Utah Utes ) and Drew Mestemaker ( Oklahoma State Cowboys ). All three quarterbacks had resumes and numbers worthy of being recognized as the nation’s best upperclassman quarterback in college football. However, the difference in stats between Mensah and Manning are staggering. Read More: Best College Football Defenses Right Now ESPN QBR Pass Yards /YPG TD – INT YPA Darian Mensah 88.6 (1st in CFB) 3,076 / 308.6 29 (9.1%) – 2 (0.6%) 9.7 Arch Manning 62.3 (63rd) 2,198 / 219.8 19 (6.6%) – 10 (3.5%) 7.6 Mensah has statistically been the best quarterback in college football this season, averaging the most passing yards per game (307.6) among the Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award finalists while ranking fourth nationally in passing touchdown rate, third in yards per attempt (9.7) and first in ESPN QBR (88.6). Both statistically and based on record (9-1 vs. 9-2), he should be ahead of Manning. At a time when there’s a growing belief among fans and even college football analysts that the College Football Playoff rankings are heavily biased toward SEC teams, this seemed like another example of conference favoritism. So, why isn’t Mensah a Golden Arm finalist? Because under the criteria set forth by the Golden Arm Foundation , a quarterback is ineligible from consideration if they’ve transferred twice. Mensah started for the Tulane Green Wave in 2024 before transferring to become a star with the Duke Blue Devils this past season. By transferring a second time to replace Carson Beck as the Hurricanes’ quarterback in 2026, he made himself ineligible for the Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award. It certainly feels like an outdated criterion given the state of modern college football, but it could also be a non-issue in the years to come if the NCAA and Power Four conferences have their way with changes to transfer rules. For now, Mensah is ineligible, and Manning inexplicably made the list despite being an average starting quarterback this season. Read more at Sportsnaut

item.title: Detroit Lions name a new captain on defense
item.description: Nov 8, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Detroit Lions safety Chuck Clark (36) runs with the ball after an interception during the second half against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As first reported by Justin Rogers and confirmed by coach Dan Campbell on Friday, the Detroit Lions have a new defensive captain. Veteran safety Chuck Clark was given the honors earlier this week, after the Lions had lost two defensive captains to injury over the past three weeks: Jack Campbell (neck), Aidan Hutchinson (knee). “It felt like the right thing to do,” Campbell said. “We obviously lost a couple of our captains. He’s really just filled the void as the season has gone on. Type of guy he is, it just speaks for itself. And he’s just grown inside this locker room, he’s a great teammate, and he’s just got leadership qualities through the room. Communication is outstanding. His production has gone up as the season’s gone up. Everybody’s got a lot of faith in Chuck. He’s just kinda one of those bell-cow guys for us right now. So he earned that, so proud of him.” Clark is in his 10th NFL season and first with the Lions. Campbell noted that they knew about Clark’s leadership qualities before they signed him to a one-year, $1.5 million deal this offseason, but you never know for sure until he’s actually in the building. Thus far, he’s lived up to his reputation. “You get around him and you see it first hand. There’s nothing fake about it. He’s just real,” Campbell said. “He’s one of those guys that people gravitate to him. He’s just got it. He’s a great communicator, same guy every day, very consistent, smart, grinder. He’s everything you really want in that type of role.” In addition to his leadership, Clark has become an important part of the gameday lineup. He’s been a steadying force in Detroit’s ever-shifting secondary, logging more defensive snaps (540) than anyone else on the team. And while his role may soon decrease with the return of Brian Branch a few weeks ago and Kerby Joseph this week, Campbell noted that they want to still use all of their safeties, Clark included. “Everybody’ got a role. We’re trying to use everybody that we can in that defensive room. So all those safeties? We want to use them,” Campbell said. “There’s a role for all of those guys. And now you get Kerby back in the fold. So we’ve got a couple of things that we can do here and have flexibility to do.”

item.title: NFL Predictions: Bears offense primed for a big day against Saints
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 19: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears passes the ball during the second half of the NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at Solider Field on October 19, 2025 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the initial spread dropped for the Chicago Bears and the New Orleans Saints, I thought, that’s a really big number . Four days ago, the 7-2 Bears opened as a 9.5-point favorite over the 3-6 Saints; it then climbed to 10.5 later that evening. It’s currently up to 11.5 (at the time I’m writing this), according to FanDuel Sportsbook , but the more I look at this matchup, the more I think the Bears will easily cover. The Bears are coming off their bye week, so they’ll be well rested and ready to make another statement. I’m not saying get ready for a 59-point explosion like Week 1, but a 50-burger wouldn’t surprise me. The running game has been criticized lately, but did you realize it still ranks number 1 in attempts and is 4th in yards per game? The Bears have a top-10 offense by most metrics while the Saints have a bottom-10 defense. On the flip side, New Orleans’ offense has been bottom-10, while the surprising Bears have been top-10 on defense. And that’s with Jeffery Simmons only being a Bear for two games. Chicago’s offense is what everyone thinks of when discussing how well-timed their bye week was, but the defense also gets a chance to self-scout and figure out how best to play off Simmons. I like the Bears’ offense starting strong on Sunday, their defense getting a few turnovers, and them winning 38 to 17. So give me all these Bears overs: Caleb Williams’ passing yards (245.5), Caleb passing touchdowns (2.5), Rome Odunze receiving yards (45.5), and D’Andre Swift rushing/receiving yards (82.5). item.title: 2026 Atlanta Braves Player Review: Elieser Hernández
item.description: ATLANTA, GA - JULY 31: Elieser Hernández #57 of the Atlanta Braves pitches in the seventh inning during the game against the Washington Nationals at Truist Park on July 31, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Matthew Grimes Jr./Atlanta Braves/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the more interesting mini-plots of the 2026 Atlanta Braves season was Elieser Hernández’s journey up and down, and all around, the Gwinnett Express. He’d come up, pitch some big innings, get designated for assignment shortly afterwards, return to Gwinnett, and do it all over again at some point down the road. It’s time to examine how this journey went for him. How Acquired Hernández inked a minor league deal with the Braves last November and began the season with the Gwinnett Stripers in Triple-A. It took Hernández all the way until late July for the Braves to call him up to the bigs and boy, did he end up coming through in a big spot for Atlanta. What were the expectations? For the first five years of his career, Hernández was an up-and-down arm with the Marlins. He did make 48 starts, 42 relief appearances, and log over 280 innings, but they came with a -0.7 fWAR. Things weren’t much better in 2024 as the Brewers and Dodgers took a brief flier on him, but he ended up pitching in Korea with the LG Twins for part of that season, as well as 2025. All that meant was that when the Braves added him back to an MLB organization after the 2025 season, the expectations were that he would provide depth for Gwinnett, with no real assumption of any kind of usefulness or quality if anyone bothered to call him up to the bigs. 2026 Results But, the Braves did call him up! Hernández pitched in his first big league game since 2024 on July 24, which is when Walt Weiss called his name in the seventh inning of a game where the Braves were trailing the Orioles by one run. Hernández then proceeded to face 13 batters and ended up clearing three innings as a result, which helped get the Braves into extra innings and eventually ended up earning him the pitcher win after the Braves broke out for four runs in the tenth inning of that one. This was a fantastic result for Hernández and his reward was getting designated for assignment and eventually electing free agency before returning to the Braves organization by July 28. By July 31, Hernández got called up again and once again, he proceeded to throw three more innings for the Braves. This time, he essentially gave the rest of the bullpen the night off after a six-inning stint from Bryce Elder by pitching the final three innings and picking up a save as a result. He did give up one run on five hits this time around, but he struck out four batters along the way and the Braves cruised to victory thanks to his efforts. item.title: Divisional Rankings: Ciryl Gane is UFC’s defending champion, but is he MMA’s true No. 1 heavyweight?
item.description: Ciryl Gane was triumphant at UFC 334 | Jeff Bottari, Zuffa LLC In the ever-shifting MMA landscape, ranking the world’s greatest fighters might seem like a fool’s errand, but that’s exactly what we’ve set out to do with the MMA Fighting Global Rankings. Here, our esteemed panel sorts out the movers and shakers from every division to provide you with the most definitive list of the best fighters on the planet. It’s official: Ciryl Gane is not only the UFC’s undisputed heavyweight champion, he’s a defending one as well. But how undisputed is he, really? Gane’s curious rise to the top of the division is well-documented. In his second shot at the undisputed title, Gane faced off with Tom Aspinall at UFC 321, but the duel ended inconclusively after Gane poked Aspinall in the eyes, rendering him unable to continue. With Aspinall having to undergo surgery for the resulting injuries, Gane was booked to fight Alex Pereira in an interim heavyweight championship bout at UFC White House in a matchup presumably made to give Pereira the opportunity to become the UFC’s first-ever three-division titleholder. History was put on hold as Gane defeated Pereira by second-round knockout ( a result that wasn’t without controversy, at least according to “Poatan” ) to become interim champion a second time. Then, in September, with no firm date for Aspinall’s return on the horizon, Gane was promoted to undisputed status and promptly booked to fight Josh Hokit in the main event of UFC 334. Gane took care of business this past Saturday, withstanding a relentless assault from Hokit to convincingly out-strike him and claim a unanimous decision victory. So he’s the clear-cut No. 1 heavyweight, right? Not so fast. As it stands, the MMA Fighting Rankings panel still has Aspinall hanging on to the No. 1 spot, though the vote was not unanimous. Aspinall and Gane both received two first-place votes each, with lineal champion Francis Ngannou claiming one as well. Let’s not forget Ngannou holds a win over Gane from their championship fight back in 2022, and Gane’s case is also hurt by lackluster performances against Jon Jones and Alexander Volkov in recent years. That said, Ngannou’s most recent win is against UFC washout Philipe Lins, and Aspinall will be subject to our 18-months of inactivity automatic removal rule if he does not return to action by April. So Gane could soon by No. 1 by default, which as we all know is the sexiest way to become recognized as the best in your field. item.title: Saints Draft Position: NFL Week 11
item.description: IOWA CITY, IA - NOVEMBER 22: Offensive lineman Kade Pieper #58 of the Iowa Hawkeyes before the match-up against the Michigan State Spartans at Kinnick Stadium on November 22, 2025 in Iowa City, Iowa. (Photo by Matthew Holst/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last season, even when the New Orleans Saints were consistently losing, their draft pick was not moving much because of how bad other teams were. This season is similar, and as of writing this, 12 teams only have 3 wins. It creates a situation where the Saints will barely move if they lose because everyone else is also losing. So, looking at their current draft position, the Saints are set to select at pick 11 overall. For this edition, I wanted to do a trade back to the mid-20s and look at the prospects there. OL Kade Pieper First, let’s start with the offensive line. Sadly, Jeremiah Wright has not secured the Saints RG spot, and Cesar Ruiz could be on his way out. Erik McCoy’s time in New Orleans may also be coming to an end soon, which would leave the Saints having to fill both center and right guard. In the draft, Iowa offensive lineman Kade Pieper would make perfect sense as an option. He was a star at RG for Iowa, becoming a first-team All-American. This season, he was moved to center and is playing well there. He will allow the Saints some flexibility, playing RG his rookie year and potentially moving to center if McCoy leaves in 2028. LB Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa Next is on defense. LB is an underrated need for the Saints with how well Kaden Elliss has played, but they need to find someone to put next to him. Investing a high pick in that position could set up the defense really well, and if Chris Cole is gone early in the first, trading back for Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa would be a great move. Viliamu-Asa can play throughout the defense, is an incredible run defender, is very athletic, and is a tackling machine. He has dealt with injuries and can be a target in the passing game, which is why he won’t be a higher pick, but at the back of the first round, he could be a really good option.

item.description: (Photo by Peter Aiken/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kansas City hosts the injury-depleted Arizona Cardinals on Sunday in what should be another very winnable game. The Chiefs are 7-2 and tied with the Denver Broncos atop the AFC West, one game behind the Buffalo Bills in the race for the AFC’s No. 1 seed. Arizona is 3-7, has lost consecutive games, and is coming off a 34-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams . After Sunday, Kansas City begins a five-game stretch against Buffalo, the Los Angeles Rams , Cincinnati , New England and San Francisco. The first three games of that stretch will be on the road, beginning with a Thanksgiving night matchup against the Bills just four days after the Cardinals game. The Chiefs cannot afford to overlook Arizona, but they should use this matchup to prepare themselves for what is coming. Here are three Kingdom Keys to a Chiefs victory. Offensive key: Keep building chemistry with the wide receivers. Kansas City’s wide receivers delivered their best collective performance of the season against Atlanta. Rashee Rice, Josh Downs, Cyrus Allen, and Andrew Armstrong combined for 12 receptions, 222 yards and three touchdowns. Rice led the group with five catches for 82 yards, while Downs caught four passes for 53 yards and a touchdown in his Chiefs debut. Allen and Armstrong also delivered explosive touchdown receptions of 39 and 43 yards, respectively. The receivers accounted for nearly 64% of Patrick Mahomes’ 348 passing yards and three of his five touchdown passes. That production must become the start of a trend rather than a one-game explosion. Downs had only two full practices with Mahomes before the Atlanta game. Sunday offers another chance to build that connection while continuing to define roles for Rice, Allen and Armstrong. It would also be encouraging to get Worthy involved after he went without a reception on three targets against the Falcons. Arizona presents an ideal matchup for that continued growth. The Cardinals have allowed 22 passing touchdowns — tied for the second-most in the NFL — and are surrendering 28.9 points per game. The Chiefs will need their receivers during the upcoming stretch against several playoff contenders. Buffalo, Los Angeles, Cincinnati, New England and San Francisco will all have defensive plans designed to slow Kansas City’s running game and force the receivers to win their matchups. Another combined 150-yard performance from the wide-receiver room would qualify as a successful afternoon. More importantly, Kansas City needs the group to keep building timing and trust with Mahomes before the schedule’s difficulty increases. Defensive key: Force Carson Beck into multiple turnovers The Chiefs’ defense has been one of the league’s best at keeping opponents out of the end zone. item.title: Darius Acuff is showing flashes of NBA stardom, but he has one massive problem
item.description: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Flip on a Sacramento Kings broadcast and you’re likely to be inundated with graphics, statistical queries or fun facts framing Darius Acuff Jr. in an illustrious ensemble. Names like Michael Jordan, LeBron James, Oscar Robertson and Luka Dončić are frequently mentioned alongside the rookie guard, who is averaging a robust 26.2 points, seven assists (3.9 turnovers) and 3.6 rebounds through the first 14 games of his career. It’s an esteemed neighborhood for Acuff to reside in and certainly an encouraging omen as he progresses further into his NBA tenure. Skeptics, however, will peek beyond the box score and point to Sacramento’s 1-13 record, Acuff’s relative scoring inefficiency (53.3% true shooting, 24th percentile, per Dunks & Threes) or his ball-dominant tendencies to downplay his raw production. They’ll note how much of the Kings’ 27th-ranked offense is channeled through him and posit his true impact pales in comparison to those All-Star-level statlines by citing a host of metrics and data. Stretching back to his sensational freshman season at Arkansas a year ago, Acuff has divided the masses with his play. The first month of his rookie campaign has done little to assuage that polarization, a reality existing independent of anything he’s responsible for but rather captures the cantankerous discourse enveloping the sports world more than ever these days. Nonetheless, there is plenty to examine, praise and critique about Acuff’s first 14 games. He’s flashed loads of promise and indicated various areas of concern as the Kings presumably build around him moving forward. So, what about his skill-set may suggest future stardom and what may offer reasons for worry in an NBA ecosystem increasingly cruel and unforgiving to smaller guards? Let’s take a look. Every star player needs a superpower. Some are more consequential or prominent than others but they all have one. Though not a star at this stage, Acuff’s superpower is his ability to maintain a live dribble wherever and whenever he desires. That may sound rudimentary. There are a horde of guards who can haphazardly dribble the air out of the ball. But Acuff makes it immensely practical. As the league continues to evolve and grow sharper fangs defensively while also upsizing its offensive hubs, dribbling — especially inside the arc or against pressure — is a bit of a lost art. So many players are unable to initiate offense while enduring full-court physicality or slalom through gap help. Acuff can. item.title: Prognostications on the Maikel Garcia and Bryce Miller trade
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - MAY 23: Cole Young #2 of the Seattle Mariners is tagged out while trying to reach third base by Maikel Garcia #11 of the Kansas City Royals during the game at Kauffman Stadium on May 23, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Mariners made a move this week that few saw coming as they sent Bryce Miller, Logan Evans, and Jose Ferrer to the lower midwest in exchange for Gold Glove winning third baseman Maikel Garcia and two fair-to-middling relievers. You can read all about the details and early analysis of the trade here and here . However, today’s post is meant to get y’all contemplating your orbs and looking into the future to see how this trade shakes out five years down the road or more. Let’s prognosticate! Here are some prompts to answer in the comments: Who ends their career with higher WAR: Bryce Miller or Maikel Garcia? Does Logan Evans become the underrated gem in this trade by having a breakout season for Kansas City in 2027 or even 2028? How will losing Ferrer effect the Mariners bullpen? Are Miller’s struggles mental, physical, both, or neither? Assuming full health or close to it, what is Garcia’s slash line for the Mariners in 2027? And how many stolen bases? As much as it pains me to give up on Bryce Miller when there is still a chance he puts together the kind of season that had me picking him as my dark horse Cy Young candidate before the 2o25 season, bringing in a Real Life Third Baseman who can also hit a bit does fill me with optimism. After all, enduring the left side of the Mariners infield in 2026 was like a viewing of “Salò.” Absolutely punishing and deeply unpleasant. No one wants to see either of those things more than once, so a healthy Garcia plus a healthy Colt Emerson at shortstop all season could make for a distinctly more enjoyable viewing experience. If Miller ends up an ace in KC, I’ll be happy for Cowboy Bryce, but hopefully the revamped infield defense is enough to overlook the regret of seeing Miller put it all together for another team. What do y’all think? Let’s hear your answers to the prompts in the comments, plus any other trade hot takes you want to share.

Ward showed some flashes during his rookie year but struggled with consistency. Playing behind arguably the league’s worst offensive line, Ward was sacked a league-high 55 times during his first season. Despite some of the struggles he endured last season, expectations were high for the Miami product entering year two. Most of Ward’s second year in the league hasn’t been much better than his first. This season, the 24-year-old has thrown just eight touchdown passes in nine games to go with a disappointing 53.3 QBR. Tennessee’s signal-caller has been the main reason why, as the talented young quarterback has played arguably his best two games of the year in back-to-back weeks. Over the course of the last two weeks, Ward is second in the NFL in completion percentage (70.9) to go with four touchdown passes and a very impressive 98.9 Passer Rating. item.title: Friday Discussion: What does the hiring of Trev Alberts mean for Michigan Football?
item.description: COLLEGE STATION, TEXAS - JULY 2:Texas A&M athletic director Trev Alberts speaks during Michael Earleys welcome ceremony on Tuesday, July 2, 2024, in College Station. Earley was appointed head coach of Texas A&Ms baseball program on Sunday, June 30. (Ishika Samant/Houston Chronicle via Getty Images) The University of Michigan has a new Athletic Director, as Trev Alberts has been widely reported to be accepting the role. Alberts is the current Texas A&M Athletic Director and has previously been at Nebraska both as a player and Athletic Director. Widely regarded as a relatively ruthless AD, Alberts is sure to bring widespread changes to Michigan athletics for as long as he’s here. Today’s discussion question is this: how will Alberts’ hiring affect Michigan football specifically? There are a few ways you can take this. Let’s start with the elephant in the room: Kyle Whittingham’s employment. It’s no secret that Whittingham is firmly on the hot seat thanks to a combination of the team’s record, his press conference performance, and his handling of the offense or lack thereof. Prior to the hiring of Alberts, the prevailing wisdom was that Whittingham likely wouldn’t be fired because there was no one in a position to do the actual firing. With the new university president not yet in place and Warde Manuel nearing the end of a lame-duck tenure, it would have taken the Board of Regents and/or a conglomeration of donors to find a way to make moves behind the scenes. All of that is thankfully out the window now as Trev Alberts’ first task on the job will likely be evaluating Kyle Whittingham and the football staff. You have to think that this is bad news for Whittingham. Not only does Michigan now have someone in place to make a firing if appropriate, but they also clearly placed an emphasis on making the hire quickly so that a move could be made. If the university didn’t intend to make a change, why else would they expedite the hiring of an AD and make the hire now? The timing seems far too convenient. Alberts also has a reputation for being ruthless. He has ruffled feathers at both Nebraska and Texas A&M by firing quite a few long-time staff members. Trev has also taken a “spend first, figure out how to pay for it later” approach. Buyouts such as Jason Beck’s and Kyle Whittingham’s certainly won’t make Alberts balk. However, certain traditions may also be at risk as Alberts will enforce his will throughout the department. There’s no doubt that Alberts is a proverbial mover-and-shaker in the college football world. He will without a doubt be the most noteworthy AD at Michigan in the past few decades. Whether that’s a good thing or a bad thing is yet to be seen. Michigan has won national championships in both football and men’s basketball in the last three years, yet somehow a departmental shake-up feels necessary. item.description: Oliver Bearman’s Haas VF-26 at Spa-Francorchamps in 2026. He will start the Las Vegas Grand Prix from the back after a string of new power unit parts. Photo: Der Alf / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0 Las Vegas qualifying tonight has to sort out a grid that is already being rearranged. Rain wiped out Thursday’s opening practice, the second hour ran on a damp track, and five drivers have confirmed grid penalties before a single qualifying lap. Away from the Strip, a French newspaper says Stellantis will shut its WEC, Formula E and WRC programmes on Monday, Toyota has confirmed Kévin Estre for 2027, and Marc Márquez starts his second MotoGP match point weekend in Portimão. The one storyline: Las Vegas qualifying sets a grid five penalties will reshuffle Thursday gave teams very little to work with. The first session was washed out, and FP2 began on wet and intermediate tyres. George Russell set a 1:47.272 at the flag to beat Pierre Gasly by 0.071 seconds, with Charles Leclerc third, Autosport reports . World champion Kimi Antonelli was eighth, and Max Verstappen finished 13th. That leaves one hour of FP3 before qualifying, and Friday is forecast to be dry . Then the penalties land. Oscar Piastri, Carlos Sainz and Lance Stroll each drop 10 places, Antonelli drops five and Oliver Bearman starts from the back, Motorsport.com reports . So the qualifying order will not be the starting order. Antonelli and Piastri both drive cars that can reach Q3, so drivers just outside the top 10 tonight could move forward before the lights go out on Saturday. Today’s schedule, from Portimão practice to Las Vegas qualifying (ET) MotoGP, Portimão: Practice, 10:00 a.m. ET (15:00 local). This session decides direct entry to Q2, according to MotoGP.com . It is the season finale, and Alisha Palmowski already won the title in Austin . Formula 1: Las Vegas qualifying, 11:00 p.m. ET (8:00 p.m. local). Saturday: MotoGP qualifying and the Portimão Sprint, then the 50-lap Las Vegas Grand Prix at 11:00 p.m. ET (8:00 p.m. local). Marco Bezzecchi’s Aprilia at the 2025 Malaysian Grand Prix. He topped Friday’s first practice at Portimão. Photo: Liauzh / Wikimedia Commons , CC BY-SA 4.0 The MotoGP title math is simple. Márquez leads Martín by 60 points and Bezzecchi by 74. A Sprint win on Saturday would seal his eighth premier-class crown, and so would outscoring Martín by two points, Crash.net explains . item.title: Yankees Birthday of the Day: Clark Griffith
item.description: 1913 Washington Senators: Manager Clark Griffith. (photo by: HUM Images/ Universal Images Group via Getty Images) Though Clark Griffith is the first man to manage the New York baseball team we now call the Yankees, his time in New York is merely one chapter in a story of one of the giants of baseball’s early history. That’s no shot at Griffith’s time in New York and his importance to the franchise. It’s just he had such an amazing life and career. He was already an accomplished hurler when he came to New York and became the player-manager of the club, in its first season in The Big Apple. And long after he hung up his cleats, he remained an integral part of baseball in the first half of the 20th century. Clark Calvin Griffith Born: November 20, 1869 (Clear Creek, MO) Died: October 27, 1955 (Washington, DC) Yankees Tenure: 1903-07 (player/manager), 1908 (manager) Clark Griffith was already a grizzled veteran when American League President Ban Johnson named him manager of the New York Highlanders (often called the Americans in the press) prior to the 1903 season. It was the inaugural campaign for the club, which relocated from Baltimore after the Orioles folded following two seasons. The diminutive Griffith (listed at 5-foot-6) was a right-handed pitcher, and a good one, at that. Between 1894 and 1901, he won at least 20 games in a season seven times. His first season in New York was also his last one as a starting pitcher, and he tossed more than 200 innings while managing the club to a disappointing fourth-place finish. Griffith’s pitching days were not over, however. He transitioned to the bullpen and continued to pitch at a high level while trying to steer the Highlanders to a pennant. In 1904 and 1906, he came close, with the club finishing in second place each season, mere games from wining the American League. Modern Yankee fans are used to skipper Aaron Boone getting himself tossed from games, though he was shockingly well-behaved in 2026. He’s far from the first Yankee manager to get the hook, of course. Griffith, by virtue of being the first manager, gets that honor. Like his modern successor, Griffith also got himself suspended for his conduct toward umpires. On Monday, August 27th, 1906, Griffith took umbrage with a safe call at first base while playing St. Louis. As a result, the umpires ordered Griffith off the field. The Highlanders’ skipper took his sweet time about it. Unfortunately for him, AL President Johnson was in the crowd, and the next day he suspended Griffith indefinitely. Yeesh. “Savages in the Box,” this was not. Seems a little harsh. But wait — there’s more. The indefinite suspension might have something to do with Griffith fighting umpire Tim Hurst earlier in the season, which also got him suspended. For that round of fisticuffs, Griffith received a five-day suspension. His ban in August lasted a week. The Highlanders bottomed out on Griffith’s watch in 1908, and in June he decided it was time for him to move on. Owner

item.title: Evan Mobley hosted annual gala to raise money for underserved youth
item.description: CLEVELAND — Evan Mobley’s upbringing was slightly unconventional. His parents regularly opened their home to foster children and foreign exchange students while he and his brother Isaiah were growing up. That generosity has stayed with the Cleveland Cavaliers ’ forward all these years later. “I feel like my parents just instilled that into me, and I feel like it just comes natural to give back and help people,” Mobley said. “Bring them into your world and trying to bring them up with you. I’ve done that since I was a kid just because that’s how we grew up.” Evan, in partnership with his brother Isaiah, launched The Mobley Foundation in 2025 to accomplish this mission. The foundation aims to empower “ underserved youth to become well-rounded, contributing members of their communities .” They do that through their four pillars of: financial fitness, physical fitness, mental and emotional fitness, and academic and career fitness. On Thursday, The Mobley Foundation held its second annual “Beyond the Game Gala” downtown. This was a fundraiser that included a fine dining experience, a silent auction with several impressive items and experiences, and a chance to mingle with Cavs players. Having his teammates, coaching staff, and the front office come to the event is one of the biggest highlights for those who’ve paid to attend. The attendees are given a basketball and a chance to get as many of the players to sign it as they can. Having nearly everyone in the organization back him up in this endeavor is meaningful for Mobley. “It means a lot,” Mobley said. “We had a very busy week with a lot of events. All the staff, all the player are all here to support me and my foundation. It means a lot.” The team’s attendance and willingness to get behind Mobley will help the foundation immensely. Proceeds from the gala are going to help local foster kids have a Christmas they won’t forget. For the last two years, Mobley has brought local foster kids to Walmart for a holiday shopping trip . They’re doing one again next month. “We’re going to expand it and grow it even more,” Mobley said. “I’m not sure of the numbers of how many kids yet, but we’re going to keep expanding that and keep making it bigger just to give back to families that don’t necessarily get the holiday cheer.” “Christmas is my favorite holiday,” Mobley continued. “For people that don’t necessarily get that, it just brings them so much joy.” This is just the start for The Mobley Foundation in its second year. The goal is to continue expanding its reach and impact for years to come. “I’m not sure where it will be in five or 10 years, but we just hope that it gets bigger and bigger, where we can help as many kids and families that need it,” Mobley said.

item.title: Arsenal has an offside problem that is not being talked about
item.description: Arsenal has an offside problem that is not being talked about Arsenal remain one of the strongest teams in world football, as their position at the top of the Premier League table and continued performances in the Champions League demonstrate. Mikel Arteta’s side has shown their ability to compete at the highest level and has overcome significant challenges in recent seasons. However, despite their success, one criticism that continues to follow the Gunners concerns their lack of goals. They have not always been prolific in front of goal, and their ability to win matches by narrow margins has sometimes overshadowed the need to improve their attacking output. Arsenal’s attacking efficiency remains a concern Arsenal’s defensive strength means that they do not always need to score several goals to secure victories. Their organisation at the back often allows them to protect a narrow advantage, making a 1-0 result enough to collect three points . That does not mean, though, that the team have stopped trying to create more opportunities or increase their goal tally. The Gunners remain among the sides that create plenty of chances, but their attacking moves do not always end with a goal attempt. One recurring problem has been players getting caught offside, which brings promising attacks to an end before they can produce a scoring opportunity. That issue has become particularly noticeable this season, with Arsenal recording a high number of offside decisions against them. It is an area that could be costing them chances to turn their attacking pressure into more goals. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) Offside figures highlight an issue for Arteta According to Opta Stats via Sports Mole , Arsenal have had 35 offside calls against them this season. That is 11 more than the next Premier League team, leaving the Gunners clearly ahead of their rivals in this particular statistic. The figure works out at an average of 3.5 offside decisions per match. The report also adds that this is the highest number recorded by a team since the 2008/2009 season, highlighting the scale of the problem. Arteta will want his players to address the issue as the campaign continues. Better timing of runs and greater awareness of defensive lines could help Arsenal make more of the chances they create. item.title: 'No-one is going to break us' - defiant Boks face Ireland without Erasmus
item.description: Siya Kolisi (right) spoke passionately about what rugby means to South African people in his pre-match news conference [Getty Images] Already circled as one of the must-see fixtures in a packed November schedule, interest in the meeting between Ireland and South Africa has intensified following their contrasting disciplinary fortunes in recent days. Not for the first time, Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus landed himself in hot water with the powers-that-be for criticising match officials. After receiving a six-match ban for questioning the integrity of referee Andrea Piardi and television match official Matteo Liperini in South Africa's defeat by France last week, Erasmus has been defended and condemned . Any doubt about where his players stand, however, was cleared up by captain Siya Kolisi, who bristled at a suggestion Erasmus was being "dramatic". "It might sound dramatic to you, but to us it means so much more," Kolisi said during his pre-match news conference. "Rugby has done a lot for our country, and it's done a lot for many of us who come from South Africa. "We know how happy people are and what the mood is like when we win, and when we lose, it gets tough. People care a lot about it. "When we play, we think about the people back home. We don't take representing the country lightly because we represent every single person in South Africa when we put on that jersey." While Erasmus has dominated headlines this week, he will not be in attendance at Aviva Stadium on Saturday. Instead, in a bizarre twist, the two-time World Cup winner will host a watchalong of the game from the team's Dublin hotel, with the conditions of his suspension prohibiting him from matchday contact with players and management. "He's been hands-on with our team [in the build-up], and we're in a good space," assistant coach Mzwandile Stick said of Erasmus. "Irrespective of what has happened, we love him, we appreciate him, and no-one is going to break us. I can tell you that for sure." Whether or not Jasper Wiese joins Erasmus' stream remains to be seen. The back row was hit with a four-match ban for a dangerous ruck clearout against France. While Wiese's fate did not attract the same level of scrutiny, South Africa's sense of injustice will perhaps be fuelled by the sight of Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast on Saturday. As predicted by Erasmus , Prendergast was cleared to face the world champions after being cited for an alleged hip-drop tackle on Fiji back row Peceli Yato. "I will tell you now for free, if that was a Fijian player tackling an Irish player with that hip-drop, that player would be in Fiji now," said Stick. item.title: Leeds United Plan Talks With This Midfielder That Chelsea Scouted: Right Call For Farke?
item.description: Leeds United Plan Talks With This Midfielder That Chelsea Scouted: Right Call For Farke? Leeds United plan to open contract extension talks with midfielder Ao Tanaka, according to TEAMtalk journalists Graeme Bailey and James Marshment . The Japan international’s deal runs until June 2028, and with Premier League and European clubs showing interest, Elland Road wants the situation settled before anyone tests the market. Chelsea and Liverpool have scouted the 28-year-old this season, while Manchester United, Tottenham Hotspur, Monaco, RB Leipzig and several Bundesliga clubs are also monitoring him. Tanaka reportedly wants to stay, which gives Leeds a clear opening to move quickly. What Farke gets from him Daniel Farke backs the idea, and the case is easy to follow. Tanaka has been a regular starter since joining from Fortuna Düsseldorf for £2.9m in 2024, and he has started eight of his nine Premier League appearances this season, usually alongside captain Ethan Ampadu. The numbers explain Farke’s trust. Across 641 minutes, Tanaka has completed 86.4% of his passes, made 23 tackles and won 58.7% of his duels, a heavy workload for a 5ft 11in midfielder. His 11 shots have produced 1.27 expected goals without a goal, so the chances are arriving even if the finishing isn’t. There are limits. Tanaka has won only two aerial duels, and just eight of his 18 long balls have found a teammate, so Leeds lose some height and direct passing when he starts instead of Sean Longstaff or Anton Stach. Should Leeds United make Tanaka a priority? LEEDS, ENGLAND – NOVEMBER 07: Ao Tanaka of Leeds United looks on during the warm up before the Premier League 2026/27 match between Leeds United and Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road on November 07, 2026 in Leeds, England. (Photo by George Wood/Getty Images) Yes, and quickly. Leeds signed a £2.9m player whom FotMob now values at about £13m, and replacing a Premier League starter at that price is harder than it sounds for a side on 14 points from ten games, six clear of the relegation zone after beating Tottenham 1-0 this month. Tanaka also suits the double pivot because his tackling and recoveries let Ampadu stay deep. The contract needs care. A three-year deal with a modest raise protects Leeds, whereas a longer, bigger package would reward a midfielder who is yet to score this season and offers little in the air. Leeds can’t treat his willingness to stay as permanent either, because Florian Plettenberg reported in April that he was open to leaving . If talks stall into next summer, Leeds will be selling a starter with one year left, and Chelsea or Liverpool will set the price.

item.title: Three Rivers Report: The Steelers have a DK Metcalf problem

The front office answered by adding former Seahawks receiver D.K. Metcalf to the room with Aaron Rodgers as the quarterback. After signing him to a lucrative extension, Metcalf has been inconsistent, to say the least. The receiver had his issues in Seattle, but after a contract extension, the Steelers should be concerned about Metcalf and his future with the team. From an analytical standpoint, Metcalf is 45th (!!) in the NFL with an EPA/target of 0.05. For reference, he’s tied with Laquan Treadwell and just ahead of Eagles receiver Makai Lemon. Another troubling data point is the 19 contested targets for Metcalf, which is good for ninth in the NFL. Now, that isn’t exactly a black-and-white metric, but you’d hope to see more separation. As far as targeted success rate, Metcalf sits at 38.6%. Playing receiver is twofold, as the quarterback has to deliver the football, and Rodgers has a 61.4% on-target rate when targeting Metcalf. The drops have been discussed and can’t happen, but with only 432 receiving yards, it’s hard not to be concerned about his future with the potential quarterback change next season. item.title: The Best Lazio Kits of All Time
item.description: The Best Lazio Kits of All Time It may not be the first club that’s brought up when discussing greatest all time kits, but you’d be surprised at how many gems SS Lazio have in their kit closet. They’re currently flying high in Serie A with an incredible start to the season in Gennaro Gattuso’s first year in charge, but one of the most interesting pieces of news coming from Lazio is the fact that they are reportedly leaving Mizuno and signing with Hummel as their kit supplier for the 2027-28 season. Lazio’s most iconic kits came during their time with Umbro and PUMA through the ’90s, ’00s, and early ’10s, before the club moved on to Macron in 2012 and Mizuno 10 years later. Overall, Lazio’s kit history has had its ups and downs, or to quote Gattuso’s iconic press conference line from 2014 , “Sometimes maybe good, sometimes maybe shit.” However, when you dig deeper and appreciate the kit history of SS Lazio, you really find and appreciate some of the gems they’ve had. Their portfolio of shirts certainly isn’t talked about in the same way Milan, Juventus or Inter’s are. So what will Hummel bring, aside from a reported £5 million to take over from Mizuno? The Dutch brand has a longstanding reputation for iconic kits that have careful and meaningful design. Mizuno, while having a lot of strong points in its catalogue, didn’t flex its muscles much with Lazio’s kits. Hummel, to me, seems more likely to do so. He also said some of the criticism was "fair". However, he feels some of it has gone too far. "Being in this position comes naturally with the criticism and scrutiny we're going to get," he said. item.title: Baltimore Ravens deactivate Marlon Humphrey for Carolina game after ‘criminals’ remark about Baltimore
item.description: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 16: Marlon Humphrey #44 of the Baltimore Ravens looks on from the sideline during the second half against the Los Angeles Chargers at M&T Bank Stadium on November 16, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) Baltimore coach Jesse Minter says the veteran cornerback will miss Sunday’s game after describing criminals as one of the city’s top products on his podcast. The Baltimore Ravens have deactivated cornerback Marlon Humphrey for their upcoming game against the Carolina Panthers after comments he made about Baltimore on his podcast triggered backlash from city officials and residents. Head coach Jesse Minter announced Thursday, November 19, that Humphrey had been sent home and would not practice for the remainder of the week. Minter described the decision as a one-game deactivation, saying the organization wanted to address remarks that did not reflect its relationship with the city. Humphrey, who is in his 10th NFL season, had said on his podcast that Baltimore was best at making “criminals,” adding that the comment would likely be edited out. According to Associated Press, Humphrey apologized for the remark on Wednesday, but Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott said a verbal apology was “not enough.” Getty Images Brandon Scott also appeared to criticize Humphrey’s recent performances, suggesting that prominent Baltimore residents could similarly use their platforms to question whether the city still produces great defensive backs. Minter said Marlon Humphrey was remorseful and understood the impact his words could have on people in Baltimore. “When you say something like that, it’s not a reflection of our team and our organization and how we want to operate,” the coach said. Ravens offensive tackle Ronnie Stanley, who has played alongside Humphrey throughout his Baltimore career, said he was surprised by the choice of words. “I know Marlon, and I know his heart. I know how much he cares about the city of Baltimore,” Stanley said, adding that the cornerback needed to be careful about how he expressed himself. Defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver also addressed the incident. “You have freedom of speech. You can say what it is you want to say, on your phone, on your platform, whatever that is,” Weaver said. “But that doesn’t give you freedom of consequence.” Marlon Humphrey is expected to return after serving the one-game deactivation, according to Minter. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
